maths_gegp2_ch01.subject: Maths
learning_objectives: Understand the concept of congruence in figures.
Identify and apply triangle congruence criteria (SAS, ASA, SSS, RHS).

concepts.name: Congruent Figures
concepts.description: Figures that have the same shape and size.

concepts.name: Triangle Congruence
concepts.description: Criteria for determining when two triangles are congruent: SAS, ASA, SSS, RHS.

concepts.name: Superimposition
concepts.description: A method to demonstrate congruence by placing one figure over another.

concepts.name: Corresponding Parts
concepts.description: Parts of congruent figures that match in position and size.

concepts.name: Parallel Lines
concepts.description: Lines that never meet and are equidistant from each other.

maths_gegp2_ch01.chapter_summary: This chapter introduces the concept of symmetry through congruent figures and triangle congruence. It covers the different criteria for triangle congruence, such as SAS, ASA, SSS, and RHS. The chapter emphasizes the importance of superimposition in demonstrating congruence and identifies corresponding parts of congruent figures. Additionally, it explores the properties of parallel lines and angles.
key_formulas_or_rules: SAS (Side-Angle-Side): If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are equal to two sides and the included angle of another triangle, then the triangles are congruent.
ASA (Angle-Side-Angle): If two angles and the included side of one triangle are equal to two angles and the included side of another triangle, then the triangles are congruent.
SSS (Side-Side-Side): If all three sides of one triangle are equal to all three sides of another triangle, then the triangles are congruent.
RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side): If the hypotenuse and one side of a right triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and one side of another right triangle, then the triangles are congruent.
real_world_connections: Architecture: Understanding symmetry and congruence is crucial in designing buildings and structures.
Art: Artists often use symmetry to create visually appealing works.
Engineering: Congruent shapes are used in various engineering designs and components.

concepts.name: Number Patterns
concepts.description: Sequences of numbers that follow a specific rule or pattern.

concepts.name: Palindromes
concepts.description: Numbers that read the same forwards and backwards.

concepts.name: Divisibility Rules
concepts.description: Rules that help determine if one number is divisible by another without performing division.

concepts.name: Magic Squares
concepts.description: Square grids filled with numbers where the sums of each row, column, and diagonal are the same.

concepts.name: Kaprekar's Routine
concepts.description: A process involving the rearrangement of digits of a number to reach a constant value.

maths_gegp1_ch03.chapter_summary: This chapter explores various intriguing aspects of numbers, including patterns, palindromes, and rules of divisibility. Students will engage with number puzzles, learn about magic squares, and discover the fascinating Kaprekar's routine. Through exercises and activities, learners will enhance their mathematical thinking and problem-solving skills.
key_formulas_or_rules: A number is palindromic if it remains the same when reversed.

Divisibility rules for 2: last digit is even; for 3: sum of digits is divisible by 3; for 5: last digit is 0 or 5; for 9: sum of digits is divisible by 9; for 11: difference between the sum of digits in odd positions and even positions is 0 or divisible by 11.
maths_gegp1_ch03.real_world_connections: Understanding number patterns and divisibility can help in various fields such as coding, cryptography, and even in everyday tasks like budgeting and scheduling. Magic squares have historical significance in art and culture, while Kaprekar's routine showcases the beauty of number manipulation.

activities_preserved.instructions: Investigate the process of reaching the Kaprekar constant using various 4-digit numbers.

concepts.name: Prime Numbers
concepts.description: Numbers greater than 1 that have no divisors other than 1 and themselves.

concepts.name: Composite Numbers
concepts.description: Numbers greater than 1 that have more than two divisors.

concepts.name: Prime Factorization
concepts.description: Expressing a number as a product of its prime factors.

concepts.name: HCF and LCM
concepts.description: HCF is the highest number that divides two or more numbers, while LCM is the lowest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers.

concepts.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
concepts.description: An ancient algorithm to find all prime numbers up to a specified integer.

concepts.name: Co-prime Numbers
concepts.description: Two numbers that have no common factors other than 1.

concepts.name: Twin Primes
concepts.description: Pairs of prime numbers that have a difference of two.

maths_gegp1_ch05.real_world_connections: Understanding prime and composite numbers is essential in various fields such as cryptography, computer science, and number theory, which have applications in security, data encoding, and algorithms.

concepts.name: Proper and Improper Fractions
concepts.description: Proper fractions have numerators smaller than denominators, while improper fractions have numerators larger than or equal to denominators.

concepts.name: Mixed Numbers
concepts.description: A mixed number consists of a whole number and a proper fraction.

concepts.name: Equivalent Fractions
concepts.description: Fractions that represent the same value, even if they have different numerators and denominators.

concepts.name: Operations on Fractions
concepts.description: Includes addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of fractions, as well as finding reciprocals.

concepts.name: Comparing Fractions

key_formulas_or_rules: To convert a mixed number to an improper fraction: (whole number x denominator) + numerator / denominator.

concepts.name: Heat vs Temperature
concepts.description: Heat is a form of energy that is transferred between systems or objects with different temperatures, while temperature is a measure of the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance.

concepts.name: Thermometers
concepts.description: Thermometers are instruments used to measure temperature, with clinical thermometers used for measuring body temperature and laboratory thermometers for various scientific applications.

concepts.name: Modes of Heat Transfer
concepts.description: Heat can be transferred in three ways: conduction (direct contact), convection (movement of fluids), and radiation (transfer through electromagnetic waves).

concepts.name: Conductors and Insulators
concepts.description: Materials that allow heat to pass through them easily are called conductors, while those that do not are called insulators.

concepts.name: Land and Sea Breeze
concepts.description: Land and sea breezes are local winds that occur due to the differential heating of land and water, affecting weather patterns.

concepts.name: Acids
concepts.description: Substances that have a sour taste and can donate protons (H+ ions). Examples include hydrochloric acid (HCl) and citric acid.

concepts.name: Bases
concepts.description: Substances that have a bitter taste and feel slippery or soapy. Examples include sodium hydroxide (NaOH).

concepts.name: Indicators
concepts.description: Substances that change color in the presence of an acid or a base. Common indicators include litmus, turmeric, and china rose.

concepts.name: Neutralization Reaction
concepts.description: A chemical reaction between an acid and a base that results in the formation of salt and water.

concepts.name: pH Scale
concepts.description: A scale that measures how acidic or basic a substance is, ranging from 0 to 14.

concepts.name: Salts
concepts.description: Compounds formed from the neutralization reaction between an acid and a base.

key_formulas_or_rules: Neutralization Reaction: Acid + Base -> Salt + Water
pH Scale: 0-7 (Acidic), 7 (Neutral), 7-14 (Basic)
real_world_connections: Using vinegar (acid) in cooking and baking.

concepts.name: Physical Changes
concepts.description: Changes that are reversible and do not form new substances.

concepts.name: Chemical Changes

concepts.name: Rusting

concepts.name: Crystallization
concepts.description: The process of forming solid crystals from a solution.

concepts.name: Indicators of Chemical Reactions
concepts.description: Signs that a chemical change has occurred, such as color change, temperature change, gas production, or precipitate formation.

science_gecu1_ch05.chapter_summary: This chapter explores the concepts of physical and chemical changes, highlighting their differences and providing examples. Physical changes are reversible and do not create new substances, while chemical changes are irreversible and result in new substances. The chapter also discusses rusting, crystallization, and indicators of chemical reactions.
key_formulas_or_rules: Rusting: Iron + Oxygen + Moisture -> Rust (Iron Oxide)
Crystallization: Solute + Solvent -> Crystals
science_gecu1_ch05.real_world_connections: Understanding physical and chemical changes is essential in everyday life, from cooking and cleaning to industrial processes and environmental science. Knowledge of rusting and crystallization can help in preserving materials and creating products.

exercises_preserved.question_text: Classify changes as physical or chemical.
Why is rusting a chemical change?
Give 5 examples each of physical and chemical changes.

activities_preserved.instructions: Place iron nails in water, oil, and air to observe the effects of moisture and oxygen on rusting.
Burn a magnesium ribbon in air and observe the bright light and white ash produced, indicating a chemical change.
Dissolve sugar in hot water and allow it to cool to form sugar crystals.

science_gecu1_ch06.subject: Science
learning_objectives: Understand the difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
Explain the mechanism of breathing in humans.
Identify the parts of the human respiratory system.
Describe how different organisms breathe.
Analyze the effect of exercise on breathing rate.

concepts.name: Cellular Respiration
concepts.description: The process by which cells convert glucose and oxygen into energy, carbon dioxide, and water.

concepts.name: Breathing Mechanism
concepts.description: The process of inhaling and exhaling air, involving the diaphragm and other respiratory structures.

concepts.name: Human Respiratory System
concepts.description: The system in humans that facilitates breathing, including nostrils, trachea, lungs, diaphragm, and alveoli.

concepts.name: Breathing in Other Animals
concepts.description: Different mechanisms through which various organisms, such as fish and insects, obtain oxygen.

concepts.name: Breathing Rate and Exercise
concepts.description: The relationship between physical activity and the rate of breathing in humans and other organisms.

science_gecu1_ch06.chapter_summary: This chapter explores the process of respiration in organisms, detailing the differences between aerobic and anaerobic respiration, the mechanics of human breathing, and the respiratory systems of various animals. It emphasizes the importance of respiration for energy production and how physical activity influences breathing rates.
key_formulas_or_rules: Aerobic respiration: Glucose + Oxygen -> Carbon Dioxide + Water + Energy
Anaerobic respiration: Glucose -> Lactic Acid + Energy (in humans) or Ethanol + Carbon Dioxide + Energy (in yeast)
real_world_connections: Understanding respiration helps in comprehending how exercise affects our body.
Knowledge of respiratory systems aids in the study of environmental adaptations in animals.
Awareness of anaerobic respiration is crucial in fermentation processes in food production.

exercises_preserved.question_text: Why do we breathe faster during exercise?
Name the parts of human respiratory system.

activities_preserved.instructions: Record your breathing rate before and after performing a physical activity for a set duration.

activities_preserved.activity_name: Model Lungs Using Balloons and Bottle
activities_preserved.instructions: Create a model of human lungs using balloons to demonstrate how the diaphragm works.
Conduct an experiment to observe the process of anaerobic respiration in yeast by measuring gas production.

social_gees1_ch01.subject: Social Science
learning_objectives: Understand the concepts of latitude and longitude.
Identify the significance of the Prime Meridian and the International Date Line.
Explain the concept of time zones and their importance.
Learn how to determine Indian Standard Time (IST).
Use coordinates to locate places on a globe.

concepts.name: Latitude
concepts.description: The distance of a place north or south of the Equator, measured in degrees.

concepts.name: Longitude
concepts.description: The distance of a place east or west of the Prime Meridian, measured in degrees.

concepts.name: Prime Meridian
concepts.description: The meridian at 0 degrees longitude, which serves as the starting point for measuring longitude.

concepts.name: Time Zones
concepts.description: Regions of the Earth that have the same standard time.

concepts.name: International Date Line
concepts.description: An imaginary line that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole and demarcates one calendar day from the next.

social_gees1_ch01.chapter_summary: This chapter introduces the concepts of latitude and longitude, explaining their significance in locating places on Earth. It covers the Prime Meridian, International Date Line, and the Equator, as well as the Tropic of Cancer, Tropic of Capricorn, and the Arctic and Antarctic circles. The chapter also discusses the importance of time zones and how Indian Standard Time is determined.
key_formulas_or_rules: Latitude is measured in degrees north or south of the Equator.
Longitude is measured in degrees east or west of the Prime Meridian.
Each time zone generally represents a difference of one hour.
real_world_connections: Understanding latitude and longitude is essential for navigation and mapping.
Time zones affect international travel and communication.
Geographical coordinates are used in GPS technology.

exercises_preserved.question_text: What is the importance of the Prime Meridian?
Why do we need standard time?

activities_preserved.activity_name: Locate cities on globe using coordinates
activities_preserved.instructions: Use the given coordinates to find and mark the locations of specified cities on the globe.
Choose two countries and calculate the time difference based on their respective time zones.

social_gees1_ch02.subject: Social Science
learning_objectives: Understand the concept of lithospheric plates and their movements.
Explain the processes of earthquakes and volcanoes.
Differentiate between physical, chemical, and biological weathering.
Describe the processes of erosion and deposition and their impact on landforms.
Illustrate the rock cycle and its significance in the Earth's processes.

concepts.name: Lithospheric Plates
concepts.description: The large, rigid pieces of the Earth's lithosphere that move and interact at their boundaries.

concepts.name: Earthquakes
concepts.description: Sudden shaking of the ground caused by the movement of tectonic plates.

concepts.name: Volcanoes
concepts.description: Openings in the Earth's crust from which molten lava, ash, and gases are ejected.

concepts.name: Weathering
concepts.description: The breakdown of rocks into smaller pieces through physical, chemical, or biological processes.

concepts.name: Erosion and Deposition
concepts.description: Processes that involve the wearing away of the Earth's surface and the transport of sediments to new locations.

concepts.name: Landforms
concepts.description: Natural features of the Earth's surface created by various geological processes, including rivers, glaciers, wind, and sea waves.

concepts.name: Rock Cycle
concepts.description: The continuous process of rock formation, breakdown, and reformation through various geological processes.

social_gees1_ch02.chapter_summary: This chapter explores the dynamic processes that shape the Earth's surface, including the movement of lithospheric plates, the occurrence of earthquakes and volcanoes, and the effects of weathering, erosion, and deposition. It also discusses various landforms created by these processes and illustrates the rock cycle, highlighting the interconnectedness of geological phenomena.
social_gees1_ch02.real_world_connections: Understanding these geological processes is crucial for disaster preparedness, environmental conservation, and urban planning, as they influence natural landscapes and human activities.

exercises_preserved.question_text: How do sea waves shape coastlines?
Draw and explain the rock cycle

activities_preserved.instructions: Create a model volcano using baking soda and vinegar to demonstrate an eruption.
Take a field trip to a local area to observe and document signs of erosion.

social_gees1_ch03.subject: Social Science
learning_objectives: Understand the significance of ancient trade routes.
Analyze the cultural exchanges facilitated by trade.
Examine the evolution of trade systems from barter to coins.
Identify key ports and their roles in ancient trade.
Explore the impact of trade on the spread of religions.

concepts.name: Silk Route
concepts.description: An ancient network of trade routes that connected the East and West, facilitating the exchange of goods, culture, and ideas.

concepts.name: Spice Route
concepts.description: A maritime route used for the trade of spices and other goods, crucial for connecting Asia with Europe and Africa.

concepts.name: Cultural Exchanges
concepts.description: The sharing and blending of cultural practices, ideas, and beliefs that occurred through trade.

concepts.name: Merchant Guilds
concepts.description: Associations of merchants that regulated trade practices and protected their members' interests in ancient times.

concepts.name: Barter System
concepts.description: An economic system where goods and services are exchanged directly for other goods and services without using money.

social_gees1_ch03.chapter_summary: This chapter explores the ancient trade routes, including the Silk Route and Spice Route, highlighting their significance in facilitating trade and cultural exchanges. It discusses the evolution of trade practices from the barter system to the use of coins, the role of merchant guilds, and the importance of key ports in the trade networks. Additionally, it examines how trade contributed to the spread of religions and cultural ideas across regions.
social_gees1_ch03.real_world_connections: Understanding ancient trade routes helps us appreciate the historical connections between different cultures and economies, and their influence on modern trade practices and cultural exchanges.

exercises_preserved.question_text: How did trade spread cultural ideas?
Role of Indian Ocean in trade
Important ancient trade ports of India

activities_preserved.instructions: Using a world map, trace the ancient trade routes discussed in the chapter, including the Silk Route and Spice Route.
Conduct research on the history of trade in your local area, focusing on key goods traded and the impact on local culture.

social_gees1_ch04.subject: Social Science
learning_objectives: Understand the differences between rural and urban settlements.
Identify factors that influence the location of settlements.
Explore various types of rural settlement patterns.
Discuss the causes and effects of urbanization.
Analyze the challenges faced by urban areas.

concepts.name: Rural vs Urban Settlements
concepts.description: Understanding the characteristics that differentiate rural and urban areas.

concepts.name: Factors Affecting Settlement Location
concepts.description: Exploring the various factors such as water, climate, and terrain that influence where settlements are established.

concepts.name: Types of Rural Settlements
concepts.description: Examining the different patterns of rural settlements, including compact and dispersed types.

concepts.name: Urbanization
concepts.description: Understanding the process of urbanization and its implications for society.

concepts.name: Census Data
concepts.description: Analyzing census data to understand demographic changes in rural and urban areas.

social_gees1_ch04.chapter_summary: This chapter provides an in-depth look at the characteristics and differences between rural and urban settlements. It discusses the various factors that influence the location of these settlements, such as water availability, climate conditions, and terrain features. The chapter also categorizes rural settlements into compact and dispersed types and examines the phenomenon of urbanization, including the development of smart cities. Finally, it highlights the importance of census data in understanding the demographic trends in both rural and urban areas.
real_world_connections: Understanding settlement patterns can help in urban planning and resource allocation.
Knowledge of urbanization trends is crucial for addressing social issues in cities.
Census data analysis aids in policy-making and development strategies.

activities_preserved.instructions: Conduct a survey in your neighborhood to identify the type of settlement pattern present and the characteristics of the area.

activities_preserved.activity_name: Compare census data of rural and urban areas
activities_preserved.instructions: Gather census data for your local rural and urban areas and compare the demographic information.

social_gees1_ch05.subject: Social Science
learning_objectives: Understand the concept of globalization and its significance.
Analyze the role of MNCs and WTO in international trade.
Evaluate the impact of globalization on local economies.
Discuss the principles of fair trade and its importance.
Explore the concept of global supply chains and their examples.

concepts.name: Globalization
concepts.description: The process of increased interconnectedness and interdependence among countries, primarily in terms of trade, culture, and economics.

concepts.name: Multinational Corporations (MNCs)
concepts.description: Companies that operate in multiple countries, influencing global trade and economies.

concepts.name: World Trade Organization (WTO)
concepts.description: An intergovernmental organization that regulates international trade and ensures that trade flows as smoothly and predictably as possible.

concepts.name: Fair Trade
concepts.description: A movement aimed at helping producers in developing countries achieve better trading conditions and promote sustainability.

concepts.name: Global Supply Chains
concepts.description: Networks that connect various production and distribution processes across different countries to deliver products to consumers.

social_gees1_ch05.chapter_summary: This chapter explores the concept of globalization and its impact on trade and exchange. It discusses the roles of multinational corporations and the World Trade Organization in shaping the global economy. The chapter also examines the implications of globalization on local economies, the principles of fair trade, and the structure of global supply chains.
social_gees1_ch05.real_world_connections: Understanding globalization helps students comprehend the interconnected nature of today's economy and the influence of international trade on local markets. It also highlights the importance of ethical trading practices like fair trade.

exercises_preserved.question_text: Role of MNCs in global economy
Impact of globalization on local businesses
Explain global supply chains with examples

activities_preserved.instructions: Choose several household products and research their origins, including the countries they are produced in and the supply chains involved.
Organize a debate where students discuss the advantages and disadvantages of globalization, presenting arguments for both sides.

social_gees1_ch06.subject: Social Science
learning_objectives: Understand the different types of media and their characteristics.
Analyze the role of media in a democratic society.
Evaluate the influence of advertising and media bias.
Promote responsible media consumption among peers.
Differentiate between news and opinion in media.

concepts.name: Types of Media
concepts.description: Explores various forms of media including print, electronic, and social media.

concepts.name: Role of Media in Democracy
concepts.description: Discusses how media serves as a watchdog and informs the public in a democratic setup.

concepts.name: Media and Money
concepts.description: Examines the relationship between media funding, advertising, and content.

concepts.name: Censorship and Media Bias
concepts.description: Analyzes the impact of censorship and bias in media reporting.

concepts.name: Responsible Media Consumption
concepts.description: Encourages critical thinking and responsible use of media, especially social media.

social_gees1_ch06.chapter_summary: This chapter delves into the various types of media, their roles in society, particularly in a democracy, and the influence of advertising and media bias. It emphasizes the importance of responsible media consumption and the need for critical evaluation of media content.
social_gees1_ch06.real_world_connections: Understanding media is crucial in today's digital age, where information is abundant and often biased. Recognizing the influence of media on public opinion and decision-making is essential for active citizenship.

activities_preserved.instructions: Select a newspaper article and identify any biases present. Discuss your findings with the class.
Collaboratively create a class newsletter that includes news articles, opinions, and advertisements.
Choose a current event and compare how different news sources report on it. Discuss the differences in coverage.
